newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila decrees wide-ranging powers for himself.
newsitem.headline: Kabila decrees wide-ranging powers for himself.

text.p: Self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila issued a decree on Wednesday giving himself wide- ranging powers to run the Democratic Republic of Congo until the adoption of a new constitution.
The decree was read out on state television on the eve of Kabila's inauguration as president of the former Zaire.
The 15-article decree said that the nation's three institutions were the president, the government and the judiciary.
"The government conducts the policies of the nation as defined by the president, it executes the laws of the republic and the decrees of the head of state," it said.
The president has the power to hire and fire members of the government and other holders of state posts, including in the armed forces.
The decree said that the judiciary was independent from the legislative and executive. It said laws currently in force would remain so except where they conflicted with the new decree.
